title: Reading
summary: 39 multiple-choice questions in 60 minutes, from a two-line notice to a C2 opinion column. You need **453** for NCLC 7. Reading is the most trainable skill, and the one where good time management alone can add points.
facts: 39 multiple choice, 4 options, one correct answer
Signs, notices, ads, emails, forms, news articles, opinion pieces
Easy to hard: A1 → A2 → B1 → B2 → C1 → C2
≈ 1½ min per item on average — but **fast on A1–A2**, slower on C1–C2
100–699. Harder questions are worth more (exact weights not public)
**453** (NCLC 7 = 453–498) — aim for ~475 on mocks for margin

format.title: What you read, level by level
format.body:
**A1–A2:** short practical texts: a sign (*Fermé le lundi*), an ad, a text message, a timetable. The question is 'who is it for / what must you do / when'.
**B1:** emails, notices, short articles about everyday life. Questions ask for **the purpose** of the text or **a condition**.
**B2:** press articles and testimonies. Questions ask for the **main idea**, a cause, the author's position.
**C1–C2:** dense argumentative texts, literary or academic style. Questions ask what the author **implies, criticises or concedes**.

format.title: Timing: where candidates lose points
format.body:
The most common reading failure isn't vocabulary: it's **running out of time** for the last 8 items — which are the heaviest.
A workable budget: **A1–A2 items (≈ 10): 30–45 seconds each** → about 7 minutes. **B1–B2 (≈ 20): about 1½ minutes each** → 30 minutes. That leaves **≈ 20 minutes for the last 9 C1–C2 items**.
Check the clock at item 20: you should have **30+ minutes left**.

steps.title: 39 texts, rising difficulty, one clock
steps.body:
Each question has its own short document. Texts get longer and harder as you go. You manage the time for the whole section — **nobody tells you to move on**.
Two rules: **read the question first**, and **protect time for the end**, where the items are worth most.

steps.q: It's question 20 and 35 minutes have passed. What does that tell you?
options: You're behind: speed up and guess faster on items you're stuck on
steps.explain: At item 20 you want 30+ minutes left for the heavier C1–C2 items. With 25 left you must speed up now.

steps.q: You're stuck on question 14 after 3 minutes. What do you do?
options: Pick the best option, flag it if the interface allows, move on
steps.explain: Every item is one answer; time spent over-checking one B1 item is stolen from a C1 item worth more.

points: Question first, then the text.
Budget: fast on A1–A2, ~1½ min on B1–B2, ~20 min kept for the last 9.
At item 20: **30+ minutes left**.
No blanks: guessing is free.

steps.title: Don't read — search
steps.body:
Most questions ask for **one piece of information**. Read the question, underline the key word mentally (a day, a price, *pourquoi*, *qui*), then **scan** the text for that spot and read carefully only there.
For A1–B1 items, reading the whole text 'properly' first wastes the time you'll need at C1.

steps.context:
**Piscine municipale** — Horaires d'été
Lundi : fermé · Mardi–vendredi : 7 h – 21 h · Samedi–dimanche : 9 h – 18 h
Cours d'aquagym le mercredi à 19 h (sur inscription).
steps.q: Le samedi, à quelle heure ferme la piscine ?
steps.explain: Scan for *samedi* → 9 h – 18 h. 21 h is weekdays; 19 h is the aquagym class; Monday is the closed day.

steps.context: Chers parents, en raison de travaux, la cantine sera fermée du 3 au 7 mars. Les enfants devront apporter un repas froid. Le service de garde du soir reste ouvert normalement.
steps.q: Que doivent faire les parents du 3 au 7 mars ?
options: Donner un repas froid à leurs enfants.
Venir chercher leurs enfants plus tôt.
Garder leurs enfants à la maison.
steps.explain: *Les enfants devront apporter un repas froid.* The *garde du soir* stays open, so B and D are wrong.

points: Read the question → find its key word → scan → read closely **there**.
Timetables and notices: match the exact day/line the question asks about.
Other details in the text are there to trap you.

lessons.title: Signs, ads and notices: the key words

steps.title: Small words, whole answers
steps.body:
Practical texts hinge on a few words:
*interdit / défense de* = forbidden · *obligatoire* = required · *sauf* = except · *à partir de* = from · *jusqu'à* = until · *sur réservation / sur rendez-vous* = booking needed · *gratuit / sans frais* = free · *tarif réduit* = discount · *hors taxes* = before tax · *en panne / hors service* = not working · *fermé exceptionnellement* = unusually closed

steps.context: Parking réservé aux résidents, sauf le dimanche.
steps.q: Qui peut se garer ici le dimanche ?
steps.explain: *Sauf le dimanche* = the residents-only rule doesn't apply on Sunday → anyone can park.

steps.context: Consultation sans rendez-vous du lundi au vendredi, de 8 h à 11 h. L'après-midi, sur rendez-vous uniquement.
steps.q: Vous voulez voir le médecin mardi à 15 h. Que devez-vous faire ?
options: Appeler après 11 h pour venir le matin.

steps.context: Soldes : –30 % sur tous les manteaux, à partir du 15 janvier, dans la limite des stocks disponibles.
options: La réduction dure tant qu'il reste des articles.
La réduction est réservée aux membres.
La réduction se termine le 15 janvier.
steps.explain: *Dans la limite des stocks disponibles* = while stocks last. *À partir du 15* = from the 15th, not until (D).

points: *sauf* = except · *à partir de* = from · *jusqu'à* = until.
*sur rendez-vous / sur réservation* = you must book.
*dans la limite des stocks* = while stocks last.
Read the tiny words twice — they decide A1–B1 items.

steps.title: Word match = warning sign
steps.body:
From B1, the correct option **reformulates** the text. An option that copies a phrase from the text is often a trap: it uses the text's words to say something the text doesn't say.
Ask: **is this true according to the text?** — not *is this phrase in the text?*

steps.context: Depuis l'ouverture de la nouvelle ligne de tramway, le nombre de voitures dans le centre a baissé de 15 %, selon la mairie. Les commerçants, eux, attendent encore de voir l'effet sur leurs ventes.
options: La circulation automobile a diminué dans le centre.
Les ventes des commerçants ont baissé de 15 %.
Les commerçants sont satisfaits du tramway.
steps.explain: *Le nombre de voitures a baissé* = *la circulation a diminué*. B steals '15 %' and 'commerçants' but the text says their effect is **not yet known**.

steps.context: La bibliothèque teste l'ouverture le dimanche pendant trois mois. Si la fréquentation est suffisante, ce nouvel horaire sera maintenu toute l'année.
steps.q: À quelle condition l'ouverture le dimanche sera-t-elle maintenue ?
steps.explain: *Si la fréquentation est suffisante* = if enough people come = *s'il vient assez de visiteurs*.

points: Correct options **reformulate**.
Options that copy the text's words often twist its meaning.
Test each option: *true according to the text?*

lessons.title: Emails and letters: why was it written?

steps.title: Find the purpose in the first and last lines
steps.body:
Messages are written **to do something**: invite, thank, complain, apologise, ask, inform, remind, cancel. The purpose is usually in the **first sentence after the greeting** (*Je vous écris pour…*) or the **last request** (*Pourriez-vous… ?*).
Purpose verbs to know: *se plaindre* (complain), *remercier*, *s'excuser*, *rappeler* (remind), *annuler*, *confirmer*, *demander des renseignements*.

steps.context: Madame, je me permets de vous relancer au sujet de ma demande de remboursement du 12 mars, restée sans réponse. Je vous serais reconnaissant de me tenir informé rapidement.
options: Pour rappeler une demande qui n'a pas reçu de réponse.
steps.explain: *Relancer* = follow up / remind. *Restée sans réponse* = unanswered. It's not the first request (B).

steps.q: *Je tenais à vous faire part de mon mécontentement* signals that the writer wants to…
steps.explain: *Mécontentement* = dissatisfaction; *faire part de* = let someone know → a complaint.

points: Purpose = first line after the greeting, or the final request.
*relancer* = follow up · *se plaindre* = complain · *faire part de* = inform.
Distinguish first request vs reminder vs thanks.

steps.title: Title, first sentence, last sentence
steps.body:
For B2 articles, a question like *Quel est le sujet principal ?* or *Que montre cet article ?* is answered by the **title + first sentence + conclusion**. A true detail from the middle of the text is **not** the main idea — and it's a favourite distractor.
For detail questions, go back to scanning.

steps.context:
**Le vélo gagne du terrain en hiver**
À Montréal, de plus en plus de cyclistes roulent toute l'année, même par –15 °C. La ville déneige désormais 700 km de pistes. Pour les associations, ce succès montre que les habitudes changent quand les infrastructures suivent.
options: Les aménagements encouragent l'usage du vélo toute l'année.
La ville déneige 700 km de pistes.
Il fait –15 °C à Montréal en hiver.
Les associations de cyclistes sont nombreuses.
steps.explain: Title + conclusion: *les habitudes changent quand les infrastructures suivent*. B and C are true details, not the main idea.

points: Main idea = title + first + last sentence.
A true detail is not the main idea.
Main-idea options are usually more **general** than detail options.

steps.title: Follow the connectors
steps.body:
Opinion texts present an idea, then qualify or reject it. The author's position is where the text **lands**:
*Certes / Il est vrai que / Sans doute… **mais / cependant / pourtant**…* → the view is after *mais*.
*On pourrait croire que… **Or**…* → *or* introduces the author's correction.
*Loin de…* = far from (the opposite is true). *Encore faudrait-il…* = it would still be necessary to… (a doubt).

steps.context: On présente souvent le travail de nuit comme un choix subi et pénible. Pourtant, de nombreux infirmiers de nuit affirment préférer ces horaires : moins de réunions, plus d'autonomie et une équipe très soudée.
steps.q: Quelle idée l'auteur met-il en avant ?
options: Le travail de nuit a aussi des avantages pour certains.
Le travail de nuit est toujours pénible.
Les infirmiers de nuit sont mal payés.
Il faut supprimer le travail de nuit.
steps.explain: *On présente souvent…* = the common view. *Pourtant* = the author's correction.

steps.context: Loin de ralentir les chantiers, la nouvelle procédure en ligne a réduit de moitié le délai d'obtention des permis de construire.
steps.q: Selon le texte, la procédure en ligne…
options: a supprimé les permis de construire.
steps.explain: *Loin de ralentir* = far from slowing down → the opposite: it halved the waiting time.

steps.context: Le ministre assure que la réforme est purement technique ; elle n'en modifie pas moins profondément l'accès aux bourses étudiantes.
options: La réforme a des effets importants, malgré ce qu'affirme le ministre.
La réforme supprime toutes les bourses.
Le ministre s'oppose à la réforme.
steps.explain: *N'en… pas moins* = nonetheless. The minister calls it technical, **yet** it deeply changes access to grants. C goes further than the text.

points: The view is after *mais / pourtant / cependant / or*.
*Loin de* + X = the opposite of X.
*N'en… pas moins* = nevertheless.
Wrong C1 options often **overstate** the author.

lessons.title: Traps: absolute words and what the text doesn't say

steps.title: Three traps
steps.body:
1. **Absolute words** in options: *toujours, jamais, tous, aucun, uniquement, seulement*. If the text says *souvent* or *la plupart*, the absolute option is wrong.
2. **Not in the text**: an option can be true in real life but not stated. Answer from the text only.
3. **Half-right**: the first half matches, the second half contradicts. Read every option to the end.

steps.context: La plupart des participants ont trouvé la formation utile, même si certains l'ont jugée trop courte.
options: La majorité a apprécié la formation.
Tous les participants ont apprécié la formation.
Personne n'a trouvé la formation trop courte.
La formation a été jugée inutile.
steps.explain: *La plupart* = most, not *tous* (B). *Certains l'ont jugée trop courte* rules out C.

steps.context: Le musée propose des visites guidées en français et en anglais le samedi.
steps.q: Quelle affirmation est vraie selon le texte ?
options: On peut faire une visite guidée en anglais le samedi.
Le musée est fermé le dimanche.
Il n'y a des visites que le samedi.
steps.explain: B and C aren't mentioned. D uses an absolute (*que le samedi*) the text doesn't state — it only says they happen on Saturday.

points: Absolute words (*tous, jamais, uniquement*) → check the text says exactly that.
Answer only from the text, not from real-world knowledge.
Read every option to the end: half-right is wrong.

mistakes.title: Reading every text in full before the question
mistakes.why: It eats the time you need for the C1–C2 items at the end.
mistakes.fix: Question first, then scan for its key word. Read closely only where the answer is.

mistakes.title: Running out of time on the last items
mistakes.why: The last 9 items are the heaviest — losing them costs the most.
mistakes.fix: Check the clock at item 20: 30+ minutes left. Guess and move on when stuck beyond 2 minutes.

mistakes.title: Picking the option that copies the text
mistakes.why: Distractors recycle the text's words; correct options paraphrase.
mistakes.fix: Test meaning: *is it true according to the text?*

mistakes.title: Choosing a true detail as the main idea
mistakes.why: The detail is in the text, so it feels safe.
mistakes.fix: Main idea = title + first + last sentence; it's the most general option that fits.

mistakes.title: Ignoring *sauf, uniquement, à partir de*
mistakes.why: One small word flips the answer on A1–B1 notices.
mistakes.fix: Circle (mentally) every restriction word in practical texts.

mistakes.title: Answering from general knowledge
mistakes.why: An option can be true in real life but not stated in the text.
mistakes.fix: If you can't point to the sentence, it's not the answer.

mistakes.title: Missing the turn after *pourtant / or / mais*
mistakes.why: The author sets up a view to reject it.
mistakes.fix: In opinion texts, the position is where the text lands — after the connector.

mistakes.title: Leaving blanks
mistakes.why: A blank scores zero; a guess doesn't lose anything.

checklist: Read the **question first**; find its key word; scan; read closely there.
A1–A2 items: 30–45 seconds each. Don't over-check.
At item 20: **30+ minutes left**, or speed up.
Main-idea questions: title + first + last sentence.
Opinion texts: the view is after *mais / pourtant / or*.
Stuck for 2 minutes? Best guess, move on. Never leave a blank.
